clue.text: Eccentric bathes in spirit!

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters of the following words are set out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: An odd character takes a bath in a strong drink, worth an exclamation mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' looks like a person; it is the anagram signal on BATHES plus IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong green aniseed liquor, an example of a spirit or distilled drink.

clue.text: Too much of pals to finish off with round of golf

indicators.note: the next piece is placed at the very end, finishing off the word
only much of the word pals is used, so its opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a round is the round letter O; 'of golf' dresses the surface

explanation.surface: Friends finishing the day with a round of golf, perhaps overdoing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Too' looks like part of 'too much' but stands alone as the definition, meaning also.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean in addition or as well, a plain synonym pair.

clue.text: Hinder the continuity of one's main ancestral line

definitions.meaning: to check a flow, as in staunching bleeding
the main line of descent of a family, its stock

explanation.surface: Something that breaks the line of descent in one's family.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to check a flow; the noun is a family's main line of descent, as in a family tree.

clue.text: Could wine be drunk by new arrival?

indicators.note: drunk means tipsy and disordered, so the letters of wine be are jumbled

explanation.surface: Might a newcomer have been drinking the wine?
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' reads as swallowed but is the anagram signal; 'Could' and 'by' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal word for a novice or newcomer to a place or activity.

clue.text: Emperor replaced his allies with ease

indicators.note: the letters are placed again in a new order

explanation.surface: A ruler easily swapped out his partners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' rearranges HIS ALLIES plus EASE; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Haile Selassie was the last Emperor of Ethiopia, ruling until 1974.

clue.text: United said to be finished a while ago

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: something finished long since is well dead

explanation.surface: A football club, United, reported as a spent force long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well dead' spoken quickly sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal pieces fused together are joined into one, which is a synonym of united.

clue.text: Put in practice a duty involving Her Majesty

indicators.note: involving means enclosing, so one piece is wrapped around the other

parts.note: excise is a tax or duty on goods
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A royal task carried out as a practice drill.
explanation.walkthrough: Her Majesty is the crossword's standard royal cipher of Elizabeth Regina; excise is a tax on goods made at home.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise a right or skill is to use it actively, putting it into practice.

clue.text: She goes over the top to get role of Titania

definitions.meaning: a person given to exaggerated, theatrical behaviour
Titania is the fairy queen in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, a play's royal role

explanation.surface: An actress overplays her part as Titania.
explanation.walkthrough: Titania is a queen in a drama, read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: An overreacting, histrionic person; and literally a queen in a play, as Titania is.

clue.text: Dances tend to be moved one further down the line

indicators.note: the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Dancers tend to shift one place further along a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be moved' rearranges DANCES TEND.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone later in a family line, an offspring of an ancestor.

clue.text: Small gardens here a little bit out of place

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
Kew Gardens are the botanic gardens in west London
a whiff is a faint trace, a little bit

explanation.surface: Small garden plots slightly askew.
explanation.walkthrough: KEW is the Royal Botanic Gardens in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquial British term meaning askew or awry, not straight.

clue.text: Product mechanisms often in place in pubs

parts.note: fruit is a product or result, as in the fruit of one's labours
machines are mechanisms

explanation.surface: Products and devices commonly installed in pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: These are British gambling slot machines, often found in pubs, so the definition is a description.
explanation.definitionFit: Gambling slot machines showing symbols of cherries and lemons are a standard fixture of British bars.

clue.text: Almost every other component follows past tests

indicators.note: the alternate letters come after the previous piece

parts.note: ex means former or past, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: every other component letter of the word is taken, skipping the rest

explanation.surface: Nearly every alternate part comes after old tests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' looks like a modifier of 'every', but it is the word whose odd-numbered letters are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Short form of examinations, formal tests of knowledge.

clue.text: Rogue hurries along with cheap way to pay

indicators.note: rogue means wayward or uncontrolled, so the letters run amok

explanation.surface: A rascal rushes off with a cheap method of payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rogue' is the anagram signal on HURRIES plus CHEAP; 'along with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A British instalment plan where goods are paid for over time, a method of paying.

clue.text: Pittance provided initially to get spies back can be laid on the table

definitions.text: can be laid on the table

parts.note: a sou is an old French coin of tiny value, hence a pittance

indicators.note: initially takes only the first letter of provided
back means the word for spies is read backwards

parts.note: snoops are people who spy

explanation.surface: A paltry sum, fed to spies to bring them home, can be tabled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SNOOPS into SPOONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutlery for soup is set out on a dining table when laying places.

clue.text: Pot reported to be advertised put up cheaply

parts.note: a jerry is British slang for a chamber pot

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the word is heard not read

parts.note: billed means advertised, as on a playbill

explanation.surface: A cooking pot announced as being advertised, then built cheaply.
explanation.walkthrough: A JERRY is old British slang for a chamber pot; BILLED spoken sounds like BUILD.
explanation.definitionFit: To build shoddily with poor materials, i.e. erect a house on the cheap.

clue.text: It gets heated when weird group ousts leader

indicators.note: the group throws out its first letter, its leader

parts.note: a coven is a group of witches, weird in the old sense of fateful

explanation.surface: A strange group gets heated after kicking out its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weird' recalls the Weird Sisters, Macbeth's witches; COVEN loses C.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen appliance warmed up for baking and roasting.

clue.text: Killers hated working on the side

indicators.note: working means being worked over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a side is a team, or squad

explanation.surface: Murderers hating their job, working for the opposing team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges HATED as DEATH; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of assassins sent to kill, so a collective noun for killers.

clue.text: Test one against a note prompt

parts.note: MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test for vehicles
I is the Roman numeral for one
V for versus, against
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A test of one note against another to prompt a response.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is Britain's annual roadworthiness check for cars.
explanation.definitionFit: To spur someone into action, synonymous with the verb meaning to urge.

clue.text: Press invitation to meeting for young man after public image

indicators.note: the young man comes after the public image

parts.note: a persona is the image presented to the public
a lad is a young man

explanation.surface: A youth issues a press invitation after polishing his public image.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a press release but means a newspaper advert seeking a date.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper notice seeking a partner invites readers to meet, so a printed invitation to a date.

clue.text: Chapter head in Pride and Prejudice

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the words Pride and

explanation.surface: A chapter heading in the Austen novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chapter head' suggests a book; it is the head of a cathedral chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral chapter, the body of clergy, is presided over by this senior priest.

clue.text: Spitting Image repeat

definitions.meaning: something done twice, a second go

explanation.surface: A rerun of the satirical TV puppet show.
explanation.walkthrough: Spitting Image was a British satirical puppet show of the 1980s and 90s.
explanation.definitionFit: A lookalike is an exact likeness, and a twofold copy repeats something.

clue.text: Privileged place freely available to card players

parts.note: public means open to all
a school is a group of gamblers or card players

explanation.surface: An exclusive spot freely open to card players.
explanation.walkthrough: A British 'public school' is a private fee-paying school, hence privileged.
explanation.definitionFit: Elite fee-paying British schools like Eton are seats of privilege for their pupils.

clue.text: Said to have passed time in the jungle, perhaps

indicators.note: said means spoken aloud, so the word is heard not read

parts.note: to while away time is to pass it, so whiled

explanation.surface: Reportedly spent time out in the jungle.
explanation.walkthrough: WHILED and WILD sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals living in nature, as in a jungle, are untamed, living free; 'perhaps' marks an example.

clue.text: A garden not a place where one might study a culture medium

indicators.note: not means without, so these letters are taken away

parts.note: taken as written; the four letters run on in these words is coincidental to the parse, which works by removing the study room, not by hiding

parts.words: a place where one might study
parts.note: a den is a private study room

explanation.surface: A garden is no place for studying cultures.
explanation.walkthrough: A GARDEN minus DEN leaves the jelly used in labs.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelatinous seaweed extract on which bacteria are grown in laboratory dishes.

clue.text: Board agreement expressed in two languages

parts.note: yes in French is oui
yes in German is ja

explanation.surface: A committee reaches agreement bilingually.
explanation.walkthrough: The name joins French and German words for yes.
explanation.definitionFit: A lettered board used in seances to spell out spirit messages.

clue.text: Points to lack of showy jewellery as dignifying

parts.note: E and N, east and north on a compass
bling is flashy jewellery, so none is no bling

explanation.surface: Pointing out that going without flashy jewels is more dignified.
explanation.walkthrough: BLING is slang for flashy jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise to the nobility, or lend nobility to, so honouring or elevating.

clue.text: Dreads becoming even more unhappy

indicators.note: becoming means turning into something else, so the letters change order

explanation.surface: Fears make one gloomier still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' rearranges DREADS.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of sad, so gloomier or more sorrowful.

clue.text: Small character part for someone on the way up

definitions.meaning: the upward stroke of a lower-case letter, as in b or d

explanation.surface: A minor acting role for an up-and-coming performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small character part' suggests a bit part; it is typography.
explanation.definitionFit: In typography, the stroke rising above the x-height of a lower-case letter; also one who climbs.
